name: capture_screen
summary: Capture the whole desktop to an image file and return its path, dimensions, and size. Saves to ~/Pictures/Screenshots by default; pass output_path to save elsewhere. Requires the Screen Recording permission (a denied permission is reported with a grant hint). For a rectangle use capture_region; for a single app window use capture_window.

params.name: output_path
params.description: Where to save. An existing directory (e.g. ~/Desktop) → file created inside with a generated name; otherwise the full file path (e.g. ~/Desktop/login.png), parent created if needed. A known image extension here sets the format. Leading ~ ok. Won't overwrite. Omit for ~/Pictures/Screenshots.

params.name: display
params.description: 1-based index of the display to capture (1 = main). Omit for the main display.

name: capture_region
summary: Capture a rectangular region of the screen to an image file and return its path, dimensions, and size. Give the rectangle as x, y (top-left, in screen points; 0,0 is the top-left of the main display and negatives are allowed on multi-monitor setups) plus width and height. Saves to ~/Pictures/Screenshots by default; pass output_path to save elsewhere. Requires the Screen Recording permission.

params.name: x
params.description: Left edge of the region in screen points (0 = left of the main display; may be negative on a multi-monitor setup).

params.name: y
params.description: Top edge of the region in screen points (0 = top of the main display).

params.name: width
params.description: Width of the region in points (must be at least 1).

params.name: height
params.description: Height of the region in points (must be at least 1).

params.name: output_path
params.description: Where to save. An existing directory (e.g. ~/Desktop) → file created inside with a generated name; otherwise the full file path (e.g. ~/Desktop/crop.png), parent created if needed. A known image extension here sets the format. Leading ~ ok. Won't overwrite. Omit for ~/Pictures/Screenshots.

name: capture_window
summary: Capture a single app's window to an image file and return its path, dimensions, and size. Reads the window's current on-screen bounds via System Events and photographs that rectangle. Targets the front window by default, or pass 'window_index' (1 = frontmost). Saves to ~/Pictures/Screenshots by default; pass output_path to save elsewhere. Requires the Screen Recording permission PLUS Accessibility and Automation access (used to read the window's position); a missing grant is reported with a hint. Captures whatever is on screen at those coordinates, so an overlapping window would appear in the shot.

params.name: app
params.description: App (process) name whose window to capture, e.g. 'Safari'.

params.name: window_index
params.description: Which window (1 = frontmost, 2 = next, ...). Defaults to the front window.

params.name: output_path
params.description: Where to save. An existing directory (e.g. ~/Desktop) → file created inside with a generated name; otherwise the full file path (e.g. ~/Desktop/win.png), parent created if needed. A known image extension here sets the format. Leading ~ ok. Won't overwrite. Omit for ~/Pictures/Screenshots.
